title: Relative Tor amplitude across the Zariski and small etale sites
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Write $\epsilon_X:(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}})\to(X_{\mathrm{Zar}},\mathcal O_X)$ for the canonical ringed-site morphism with exact tensor pullback $\epsilon_X^*$, and $f_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the induced morphism of small etale ringed topoi [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence], [lem-trf-zariski-etale-functor-comparison-square]. Let $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ be arbitrary [def-pc-derived-category]. Regard $E$ as a complex of $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$-modules and $\epsilon_X^*E$ as a complex of $f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\mathcal O_{Y,\mathrm{et}}$-modules. For every pair of integers $a\le b$, $E$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ over $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$ if and only if $\epsilon_X^*E$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ over $f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\mathcal O_{Y,\mathrm{et}}$. Tor amplitude in an interval means that the derived tensor with every degree-zero module over the indicated inverse-image ring sheaf has cohomology zero outside that interval [def-pc-finite-tor-dimension-over], with derived tensors computed by K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Consequently $E$ locally has finite Tor dimension over $Y$ if and only if $\epsilon_X^*E$ locally has finite Tor dimension over $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$; on the left locality means a Zariski open neighbourhood of every point of $X$, and on the right locality is on the small etale site. No quasi-coherence, boundedness, flatness, finite presentation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text:
Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ over $x$, put $y=f(x)$, $\bar y=f\bar x$, $R=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ and $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$. The inverse-image stalk comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-stalk] and [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar] give
$$ (f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y)_x=R,\qquad (f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\mathcal O_{Y,\mathrm{et}})_{\bar x}=\mathcal O_{Y,\mathrm{et},\bar y}=R^{\mathrm{sh}}. $$
These are ring identifications: the comparisons are natural in the sheaf, so commute with addition, multiplication and the unit. The last identification is [lem-sfb-etale-zariski-module-geometric-stalk] applied to $Y$. Applied to $X$, the same node identifies the structure stalk with $A^{\mathrm{sh}}$. The induced $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$-action is through the compatible map $R^{\mathrm{sh}}\to A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality]; its neighbourhood-compatibility clause identifies this map with the one on etale structure-sheaf stalks.

source.place: 0DK7, proof: the two inverse-image ring stalks; 04HX and 03PS.

proof.text:
Represent $E$ by any complex $C$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Exactness of $\epsilon_X^*$ on all modules [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence] allows its termwise application to compute the derived object, by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. The natural module isomorphisms [lem-sfb-etale-zariski-module-geometric-stalk] commute with the differentials, so they identify the representing stalk complex with $C_x\otimes_A A^{\mathrm{sh}}$. By [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat], $A\to A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is faithfully flat. The exact scalar-extension assertion of [lem-sfb-relative-tensor-faithfully-flat-comparison] therefore gives, in $D(A^{\mathrm{sh}})$ and hence after restriction to $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$,
$$ (\epsilon_X^*E)_{\bar x}\cong E_x\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A^{\mathrm{sh}}. $$
No quasi-coherence of $C$ is involved in the cited module stalk formula.

For the $A^{\mathrm{sh}}$-complex $L=E_x\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A^{\mathrm{sh}}$, regarded also as an $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$-complex via Step 1, [lem-sfb-strict-henselization-tor-interval] says that its Tor interval over $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is exactly its Tor interval over $R$. By [lem-sfb-relative-tensor-faithfully-flat-comparison], applied to $R\to A\to A^{\mathrm{sh}}$, this is exactly the Tor interval of $E_x$ over $R$. Thus for each $\bar x$ the etale stalk has interval $[a,b]$ over the inverse-image ring stalk if and only if the Zariski stalk $E_x$ has that interval over $(f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y)_x$. Both implications use the same integers.

source.place: 0DK7, proof: 0DK0 and 0DJF; use both directions of their equivalences.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-ringed-tor-amplitude-stalk-test] to the ringed space $(X,f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y)$ and the restricted complex $E$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-ring-sheaf-tor-amplitude-stalk-test] to the scheme $X$, viewed as an algebraic space, with the arbitrary ring sheaf $f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\mathcal O_{Y,\mathrm{et}}$ and complex $\epsilon_X^*E$. Step 3 equates the two stalk tests. Every $x$ admits a geometric point above it: take an algebraic closure of $\kappa(x)$ using [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique], and the geometric-point description [def-weil-geometric-point]. Consequently the two global Tor-interval conditions are equivalent. If $X$ is empty both stalk tests are vacuous and all module sheaves are zero.

We now work locally, without choosing a bound uniform on $X$. For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction] identifies $j^*$ with restriction. The etale inverse image along $j$ is restriction by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction]; the structure ring on the slice is sectionwise the same structure ring, and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open] identifies that slice with $U_{\mathrm{et}}$. Thus [lem-trf-zariski-etale-functor-comparison-square], with $a=j$, gives $\epsilon_U^*(E|_U)\cong(\epsilon_X^*E)|_U$: apply its module comparison termwise, using exactness and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. The inverse-base ring sheaves restrict to those for $f|_U$, since both composite inverse images are left adjoints to the same composite direct image. For any site slice, exactness of restriction [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] give
$$ (K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}F)|_V\cong K|_V\otimes_{B|_V}^{\mathbf L}F|_V. $$
Here $B$ is any ring sheaf, including either inverse-base ring in the statement. The tensor comparison is the cited derived isomorphism for the localization morphism; exact restriction also commutes with cohomology by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology].

source.place: 0DK7(2), local restriction identifications; 03FH, 03S2/03S3, 03WT and the ringed-site tensor comparison.

proof.text: If $E$ has finite relative Tor dimension on Zariski open neighbourhoods $U_i$ covering $X$, Step 4 applied to $f|_{U_i}$ and Step 5 give the same local intervals for $(\epsilon_X^*E)|_{U_i}$. These opens cover on the small etale site as well [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. For an arbitrary etale object $V\to X$, their base changes $V\times_X U_i$ cover $V$; [lem-sf-site-tor-interval-restriction] preserves each corresponding Tor interval after restriction. Successive restrictions agree sectionwise by [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. This is local finite Tor dimension on the etale site.

Conversely fix a nonempty affine open $U\subset X$. By etale-local finite Tor dimension and Step 5, $K=\epsilon_U^*(E|_U)$ has a cover $V_i\to U$ with intervals $[a_i,b_i]$ relative to $B=(f|_U)_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\mathcal O_{Y,\mathrm{et}}$. The images of $V_i$ are open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map] and cover $U$ by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Quasi-compactness of the affine scheme [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] and its definition [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] give finitely many covering members $V_{i_1},\ldots,V_{i_n}$, with $n\ge1$. Put $a=\min_k a_{i_k}$ and $b=\max_k b_{i_k}$. Each selected interval lies in $[a,b]$, so each restriction of $K$ has that enlarged interval. No quasi-compactness of $X$ or $V_i$ was used.

source.place: 0DK7(2), finite-subcover argument for local finite Tor dimension.

proof.text:
For any degree-zero $B$-module sheaf $F$, the comparison and exactness from Step 5 give
$$H^j(K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}F)|_{V_{i_k}}\cong H^j(K|_{V_{i_k}}\otimes_{B|_{V_{i_k}}}^{\mathbf L}F|_{V_{i_k}})=0\quad(j\notin[a,b]).$$
These restrictions are to a covering family. For every etale $W\to U$, the base changes $W\times_U V_{i_k}$ cover $W$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]; every section of the displayed cohomology sheaf restricts to zero there, so is zero by sheaf separatedness. Hence $K$ has interval $[a,b]$ against every $F$. Step 4 for $f|_U$ gives the same relative interval for $E|_U$. Empty affine opens may use $[0,0]$. The affine opens form a basis [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], so such neighbourhoods exist around every point, proving Zariski-local finite relative Tor dimension. This completes both implications without a uniform bound on $X$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NO-f35224d7c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks 0DK7 (spaces-perfect l.3008), 0DJF (more-algebra l.17262) and 0DK0 (flat l.244, (1)<=>(3) and its proof). The item statement matches 0DK7 (1)+(2) and is unchanged. Steps 1-4 are the source's stalk chain, written for both directions. The cited nodes say what each step takes: 008H, the etale stalk, and the geometric-stalk node for all modules giving O^sh and C_x⊗A^sh. Clause (3) of the functoriality node makes R->R^sh->A^sh equal R->A->A^sh. Exactness of epsilon^* on all modules comes from derived-etale-zariski-equivalence. Both stalk tests allow arbitrary ring sheaves (09U9 ringed space, 0DJJ space). Steps 5-8 write out the 'formal' clause (2): restriction commutes with epsilon^* and with the derived tensor (all-module comparison square, localization tensor pullback, 03DJ exactness). Zariski-local to etale-local uses 08H5 restriction. For the converse, the open images of etale maps have a finite subcover on an affine, the interval is enlarged, and sheaf separatedness and the affine basis finish. New node 0DJF is correct for any R->A->B with A->B faithfully flat; I checked A=B, non-flat Z->F_p, B=0 excluded and the zero complex. New node 0DK0 is correct for any local R with L not descending; I checked the field case and R strictly henselian. Neither is a duplicate: the DAG grep for 0DK0/0DJF/0DK7, the tor/faithfully-flat ids and the blueprint all came up clean. lem-sfb-etale-tor-dimension-descent is absolute (08HF), not relative. Neither new node restates an item clause. On batch 5, the geometric-stalk node (via trf-zariski-etale-tensor-sections), the 09U9 ringed Tor stalk test and the 0DJJ space stalk test (via def-trf-algebraic-space) are generic tools outside the trace-formula and Poincare assumptions. No SGA. The 25 generic tool_uses are accepted. No changes.
